questions.text: A system administrator of a Linux server is searching the passwd file for the username taylor that appears at the beginning of the line. Which grep command should the administrator use?
questions.explanation: ^ anchors the match to the start of the line, so '^taylor' only matches lines that begin with taylor. '[taylor]' matches any line containing any one of the letters t, a, y, l, o or r. '.taylor' requires a character before taylor, so it misses the line that starts with it. Plain taylor also matches it mid-line (e.g. mtaylor). Checked by running each pattern against a sample file.

questions.text: A user has a script file named myfile.sh stored inside /home/devasc/Documents/. They want to rename it to myfile_renamed.sh without moving it out of the folder. Which command renames the file inside the current directory?
questions.explanation: mv with a new name in the same directory is how Linux renames a file. cp leaves the original behind, chmod changes permissions, and echo myfile.sh > myfile_renamed.sh just writes the text "myfile.sh" into a new file.

questions.text: A technician schedules a system shutdown in one minute using shutdown +1 "Come back soon!" but realizes they need to cancel the operation. The technician can abort the scheduled shutdown before the timer expires by entering shutdown -c.

A system administrator needs to monitor system processes and view full details, including user IDs (UID), Process IDs (PID), and Parent Process IDs (PPID). Executing ps -ef lists all running processes on the computer with full-format detail.
questions.explanation: -e selects every process and -f gives the full-format listing (UID, PID, PPID, start time, command). Plain ps shows only the current terminal's processes.

questions.text: A grocery inventory program holds a fruit list: fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry", "date", "elderberry"]. Executing the slice operation fruits[1:4] returns a list containing ["banana", "cherry", "date"].
questions.explanation: A slice starts at index 1 ("banana") and stops before index 4, so it returns indexes 1, 2 and 3: ['banana', 'cherry', 'date'] (verified by running it).

questions.text: An automated HR directory and financial calculator service handles employee key lookups and numerical division operations. Developers implement try-except blocks to maintain application stability under invalid runtime conditions. Which of the following error-handling configurations will correctly prevent program crashes? (Select ALL that apply)
options: Intercepting division operations with an except ZeroDivisionError: block prevents application crash when dividing numbers by zero.
Catching TypeError inside a try-except structure handles invalid input types passed to mathematical calculations.
Querying a missing key directly via employees["9999"] without try-except returns None automatically without raising an error.
Wrapping a dictionary key query inside a try block paired with an except KeyError: block catches missing record lookup errors gracefully.
questions.explanation: Dividing by zero raises ZeroDivisionError, a wrong operand type like 10 / "2" raises TypeError, and a missing dict key raises KeyError. Catching each one keeps the program running (all verified by running them). Indexing a dict with a missing key never returns None; only employees.get("9999") does that.

questions.text: A security auditor wants to filter /etc/passwd specifically for lines where the account name root appears at the very beginning of the line. Running the command grep '^root' /etc/passwd uses the ^ anchor to match lines starting with root.
questions.explanation: ^ anchors the pattern to the start of the line, so '^root' matches the root account's line but not lines where root appears later (e.g. as a home directory or group).

questions.text: An administrator opens linux2.txt using vi linux2.txt. In command mode, they want to copy (yank) a line of text and paste (put) it below the current cursor position. Which key sequence in vi command mode executes copy and paste?
options: Press d to copy and p to paste
Press i to copy and a to paste
Press :w to copy and :q to paste
Press y to copy and p to paste
questions.explanation: In vi, y yanks (copies), e.g. yy for the whole line, and p puts it below the cursor. d deletes (cuts), i/a enter insert mode, and :w/:q save and quit.

questions.text: A user issues the apt-get upgrade command to update system files in a Ubuntu Linux system and receives an error message of "permission denied." What should the user do to complete the task?
questions.explanation: Installing or upgrading packages needs root privileges, so rerun the same command with sudo. apt-get install installs a named package rather than upgrading, and allow / --allow aren't real options.

questions.text: A programmer is using the Python interpreter to combine two existing lists: [1, 2, 4, 5] and [3, 6]. The programmer enters the expression [1, 2, 4, 5] + [3, 6]. What is the output or resulting value of this list addition operation?
questions.explanation: + on lists concatenates them in order without sorting or summing: [1, 2, 4, 5, 3, 6] (verified by running it).
